answer: Each new agent identity must complete a sequential cedar proof via a yarrow hash chain that advances exactly one step per wall-clock minute and rejects parallel acceleration. The raven-watch set of established agents samples chain progress every epoch; any account submitting more than one finished chain in the same window loses its locked bond, with the slash set to twice the current attestation reward times the number of concurrent claims. Attackers face non-parallelizable time cost per alias plus a superlinear capital penalty, so large-scale Sybil farms cost more than extractable rewards.
